concerns.text: FR-009 conditions moderator analysis on I² > 50 %. Making the decision to run moderator tests contingent on an observed heterogeneity statistic introduces a post‑hoc analysis decision that can inflate Type I error and bias conclusions. Moderators should be pre‑specified and analysed regardless of the I² value, or at minimum the decision rule should be treated as exploratory and clearly labelled.

FR-004 requires a three‑level random‑effects meta‑analysis, yet the specification (User Story 2 & FR‑009) restricts each study to a single effect size. A three‑level model is appropriate only when multiple effect sizes are nested within studies (e.g., multiple outcomes or time points). With a single effect per study the model collapses to a two‑level random‑effects analysis, making the three‑level claim misleading and potentially causing mis‑specification of variance components.
